name: C1. Compliance tracker for small independent gas-station / AGNKS / propane-station owners (Resolution No. 315, U-Gas, equipment-life dates)
buyer: Owners of small independent AGNKS, AGZS and propane filling stations, and small fuel retailers
trigger: Cabinet Resolution No. 315 of 18 June 2026: from 1 Sept 2026 limits on old or unknown-date pressure equipment, container stations only if certified modular, double-wall tanks and auto shutdown; U-Gas registration mandatory for AGNKS; register of violators due 1 Sept 2026; phase-out plan for above-ground LPG tanks by 1 Dec 2026; Eco-Himoya cylinder inspection data to be linked to U-Gas
evidence: https://www.spot.uz/ru/2026/06/28/gas-station-safety/ (fetched: 6,196 sites inventoried, 46,737 violations, 464 stations suspended, 1,553 AGNKS registered in U-Gas); https://www.spot.uz/ru/2025/09/24/ugaz/ (U-Gas launch per search summary); https://gov.uz/ru/uzenergoinspeksiya/news/view/224797
existing: U-Gas is the state system (accounting and monitoring of gas dispensed, linked to tax and MVD). No private compliance or inspection-readiness tool found. Competitor search in Russian not run (budget exhausted).
unchecked: Number of small independent operators; whether equipment-life records and inspection certificates (service life, pressure tests, fire-safety) are the real pain; licence and inspection document list; competitor search; whether state inspectors accept third-party records

first_check.duty: Confirmed, in force. Uzbekistan Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 315 of 18 June 2026 approved minimum fire, industrial, ecological and process requirements for AZS, AGZS and AGNKS. Annex 3 covers industrial safety: gas pipelines and tanks in good order, safety valves checked at set intervals, automatic overpressure protection on compressors and pumps, and an evacuation plan. Reported document items include a licence, technical passports, working fire equipment, calibrated meters and qualified technical staff. From 1 Sept 2026 to 1 Jan 2030, pressure equipment that is past its service life or has an unknown manufacture date is restricted. Container stations are allowed only as certified modular units. U-Gas is mandatory for AGNKS. A register of violators was due 1 Sept 2026, and a phase-out procedure for above-ground LPG tanks is due 1 Dec 2026. The only penalty found is temporary suspension (464 stations). Fines not found. Oversight sits with the Industrial, Radiation and Nuclear Safety Committee, MChS, Uzenergoinspeksiya and the Ecology Committee. Related: Resolution No. 325 of 25 June 2026 moves industrial-safety state services online, and from 1 Jan 2027 automated control-system data is to be used in permits for hazardous facilities (one gov.uz Uzbek-language source).
first_check.market: The 2025 inventory covered 6,196 fuel and gas sites (AZS, AGZS, AGNKS and household-cylinder refill points). 1,553 AGNKS are under supervision and registered in U-Gas (1,459 fully connected). The number of small or independent owners versus chains or state-owned stations was not found. The sector is under stress: gas deficits limited methane stations to 6 hours a day in Jan 2026, and no permits for new AGNKS are being issued, per the Deputy PM.
first_check.competitor: No private compliance or inspection-readiness tracker for Uzbek stations was found in searches in Russian and Uzbek. Existing tools: U-Gas, the state system for gas-sales monitoring, linked to tax, MVD and Energocontrol, with Eco-Himoya cylinder data to be integrated (not a safety/equipment-life tracker). 1C:KA AZS covers accounting, warehouse and payroll for independent station networks, not safety deadlines. There may be a future risk: Resolution 325 digitises industrial-safety services and permits will use automated-control data from 2027, so state e-services could absorb part of the job. Local expert and inspection firms for pressure vessels exist as a category, but none specific to stations were identified. Benzamat-type pump automation was not confirmed.
first_check.reason: The duty is real, new and enforced through suspensions, and no private tracker was found. But the main pain is capital spending (replacing equipment, double-wall tanks, relocation), not paperwork. Recurring tasks like valve checks and service-life dates are simple calendar items. The market is small (about 6,200 sites, about 1,550 AGNKS) and its ownership mix is unknown. Gas shortages are squeezing margins, and the state is digitising industrial-safety services (Resolution 325, automated-control data in permits from 2027). The buyer can be reached through the Committee's outreach events and gas associations. Willingness to pay for software is doubtful. A done-for-you service bundled with expert or inspection firms is the more plausible angle.

challenge_check.killer: None found. Partial overlap: TRIS (metrology deadlines) and Eco-Himoya cylinder data integration under Res. 315; Res. 325 digitising industrial-safety services; planned oil and gas online-control system (draft due 1 Dec 2026).
challenge_check.reason: Nothing I found kills this candidate. The text of Resolution 315 on lex.uz has no small-business exemption. It sets recurring duties: monthly test openings of spring valves, valve checks every 6 months for tanks, metrology verification, periodic vessel inspections and hydraulic tests, signed acts, and staff attestation (stations with uncertified staff are suspended from 1 Jan 2027). Searches in Russian and Uzbek found no private tracker. The state is absorbing parts of the job: TRIS access to calibration deadlines from 1 Sep 2026, linking Eco-Himoya cylinder data, a draft online-control resolution due 1 Dec 2026, and Resolution 325 putting industrial-safety services online. The number of independent owners is unverified. Willingness to pay is doubtful because winter gas limits shut down methane stations. The score stays at 4.
